result.message: Read all 12 supplied evidence files (optimize ledger/definition/best kernel, catalog manifest/definition/oracle/correctness/timing/evaluation-contract, review_tests review/preflight/evaluate) and reviewed the exact submitted candidate (subject 2054ca72… = ledger round 3, identical to .best_kernel.py). The candidate is a legitimate Triton implementation: no torch.ops/torch fallback, no hardcoded benchmark shapes or expected values, no host synchronization, no environment mutation, and the metadata-only launch cache stores scalars keyed on shape/strides/dtype/out_size/options (no tensors or pointers). The 2x fast path is mathematically faithful to PyTorch's bilinear mapping (src=(o+0.5)*0.5-0.5 reduces to the exact 0.25/0.75 taps, with max(k-1,0)/min(k+1,IW-1) reproducing i1p), and the general flat path reproduces align_corners/no-align-corners coordinates with the real input strides. No P0 code defect found; findings are advisory per code-review policy. Important context: the accepted candidate is NOT an acceleration — geo_mean 0.3503 (final verification) with every one of the six timing workloads between 0.296x and 0.428x of the reference, and the six timing cases are exactly the only shape family (OW == 2*IW) that the specialized fast path handles. The specialization is a general ratio condition rather than a hardcoded shape, so I treat it as justified specialization, not cheating; but the un-specialized general path retains the round-1 per-lane gather design that measured ~290 ms vs 0.207 ms reference on the timing-1 geometry.
